newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower, further consolidation seen.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower, further consolidation seen.

text.p: Seoul stocks ended lower on Tuesday despite late foreign buying as views that the market was still overbought depressed sentiment, brokers said.
They said the yen's fall today shattered expectations of a rebound after a consolidation in the past two trading days.
The yen weakened in Tokyo after a senior official at Japan's Ministry of Finance said that Japan had no intention of using foreign exchange rates as an instrument of trade policy.
The composite index closed 5.77 points lower at 767.74.
"Further consolidation is likely on Wednesday," said Koh Soon-shik, a broker at LG Securities.
Trading volume totalled 39.55 million shares, compared with 38.44 million on Monday.
Decliners outpaced advancers 469 to 338, with 98 unchanged.
Brokers said most blue chips faced profit taking, while theme-backed small shares picked up.
Samsung Electronics, the world's leading memory chip maker, fell 1,500 won to 69,000 due to talks that chip prices had fallen in international markets.
But Hyundai Electronics Industries closed 900 won higher at 47,500 after hitting a low of 46,000. Brokers said late foreign buying helped Hyundai recover.
Brokers said foreign buying was also focused on KEPCO, which ended 100 won higher at 27,500 after recovering from a day low of 27,300.
The yen fell to 113.00 to the dollar in Tokyo on Tuesday from 112.50 on Monday. It touched a low of 113.41.
